citation: Mahmud R., Pallewatta S., Goudarzi M., Buyya R. (2022) iFogSim2: an extended iFogSim simulator for mobility, clustering, and microservice management in edge and fog computing environments. Journal of Systems and Software 190.
description: iFogSim2 is a toolkit for modelling and simulating resource management techniques in Internet of Things, edge and fog computing environments. It represents sensors, actuators, fog devices, cloud data centres and application modules, and its second version adds mobility support and migration management with real mobility datasets and random mobility models, microservice orchestration and dynamic distributed clustering, with use cases for audio translation, healthcare and crowd sensing. It is developed by the CLOUDS Laboratory of the University of Melbourne as an extension of CloudSim and is compatible with the latest CloudSim release and with the earlier iFogSim version; the repository was last updated in October 2025 and tagged v2.0.0. Coverage: user-defined hierarchies of devices from edge to cloud, with no fixed geographic extent; mobility datasets can place devices in real cities. Format and access: Java source and bundled JARs on GitHub, run from Eclipse or IntelliJ; free of charge under the MIT licence. Caveats: models of latency, energy and network are simplified; scalability to very many devices is limited; documentation is mainly the examples and papers. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of edge placement, resilience of distributed services when nodes fail, and emergency-response or health applications that depend on edge computing. Related records: runs on CloudSim; CloudSim Plus and SimGrid are alternatives.
